target_customer: Indonesian K-12 and university entrance test students and their parents
problem: Indonesian students need affordable, engaging exam prep for the national university entrance test.
business_model: Consumer subscription and paid live classes

founders.name: Edria Albert
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page; no bio there.

founders.name: Syarif Rousyan Fikri
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page; named CEO in a Bisnis.com search summary.

competitors.name: Ruangguru
competitors.what: Large Indonesian K-12 tutoring and learning app
competitors.traction_then: Raised funding in late 2019 per a search summary of coverage
competitors.funding_then: Large rounds in 2019 and 2020 (amounts vary by source)

competitors.name: Zenius
competitors.what: Indonesian concept based video learning and exam prep
competitors.funding_then: 20 million dollars Series A announced February 2020 per KrASIA coverage

competitors.name: Quipper
competitors.what: Online learning platform for Indonesian students

technical_complexity.rationale: Video and question bank app with animation production; hard part is content and engagement, not software.

defensibility.rationale: Content could be copied and big rivals like Ruangguru and Zenius were better funded.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbents stayed larger; Pahamify cut staff in 2022 amid the funding downturn.

market_need_then: Indonesian edtech usage surged in March 2020 with school closures, and the company claimed one in three students who sat the UTBK the prior year used it for practice (company claim).

identity.mascot_or_character: Robot assistant Mipi named on the company site
identity.visual_style: Animated concept videos and gamification per KrASIA headline
identity.voice_and_tone: Playful student oriented, Rockstar Teachers for live class

branding.brand_signature: Animated concept videos with the Mipi robot assistant

brand_strength.rationale: Names the product around Indonesian word paham (understand) per the name's form, but I found no source on the name; the site claims over 1 million users and HolonIQ named it a leading edtech in 2020.

outcome_analysis: Pahamify joined YC in W20, raised an undisclosed Series A led by Shunwei Capital in November 2020 on the pandemic edtech surge, then faced the 2022 funding downturn. Bisnis.com reported in June 2022 that it laid off staff, with the CEO citing macro conditions, and a search summary says the headline described a farewell. The site is still live with UTBK and SNBT offerings, so it continues at a smaller scale and no later round was found.
notes: The Bisnis.com article returned HTTP 403, so its content comes from a search summary: layoffs and a June 28 2022 announcement, with the headline suggesting farewell. The directory lists the company Active and the site is live, so exit is none. Competitor names come from a search summary of DailySocial's November 2020 article; the page was not opened. The name origin was not found. Aggregators give founding as 2017 to 2019; YC says 2018. Bouncewatch lists Wah Hin & Co. as an investor, unverified.
